paradoxes.text: The culminating point of coercion. Each maximal threat produced its own retreat: 'Liberation Day' became a 90-day pause in a week; the Greenland tariffs of 17 Jan 2026 were dropped at Davos on 21 Jan for a 'framework'; 'cut all trade with Spain' (3 Mar 2026) became 'Spain agreed to pay more', which Madrid denies; India's 50% became 18%; Malaysia declared its agreement void. A threat used on everyone stops being believed by anyone, and the court that struck the IEEPA tariffs removed the weapon the threats rested on. Luttwak's rule: the method that succeeds is the method the other side learns to wait out.

grand_strategy.reading: The United States in October 2026 runs the most explicit grand strategy it has published since the Cold War, and the one most at odds with its own means. The ends are written down: a hemisphere held under a Trump Corollary, trade rebalanced by tariff, China kept a rival 'within bounds', Europe's defence handed to Europeans, the Middle East managed without forever wars, migration ended. At the technical level the instruments work - the border is quieter than in fifty years, allies have pledged trillions and 5% of GDP, Maduro sits in a Brooklyn cell, Khamenei is dead. At the level of grand strategy the picture inverts, as Luttwak says it must when a strategy succeeds: coercion used on everyone reached its culminating point in a year (Davos, Spain, the Supreme Court), the allies who paid became hedgers, the war of choice against Iran consumed the year that was reserved for the hemisphere and China, and the hemisphere itself produced a Venezuela that Washington now administers. Three signals that are not rows: the NDS never names Taiwan; the USMCA was left unrenewed on 1 July without any plan for what follows; and the same government that sanctioned Rosneft is buying Russian diesel. Washington's stances read accordingly: one adversary (Iran), two rivals it talks to more than to its allies (China, Russia), and a ring of treaty allies graded reluctant not because they resist the alliance but because Washington does - the first great power in the atlas whose friction with its allies is mostly its own.

stances.note: The atlas's reference case for 'rival' (ONTOLOGY: 'the US toward China'), read from Washington: the NSS names China the near-peer whose 'predatory' practices must be ended and whose domination of Asia must be deterred by denial along the First Island Chain, and the NDS says the goal 'is not to dominate China; nor to strangle or humiliate them'. No will to destroy the other state, a chip embargo and a tariff wall held as bargaining chips, a truce extended two months at a time. Warming because three summits in eleven months (Busan 30 Oct 2025, Beijing 14-16 May 2026, Xi in Washington 23-25 Sep 2026) cut tariffs on about USD 30bn of goods, launched a Board of Trade and an AI dialogue, restored military channels and let Nvidia sell H200s for a cut; the NYT reads the turn as 'embracing it as a peer power'. Not partner: each side keeps its weapon (rare-earth licences, the affiliates rule, the arms package to Taiwan 'in abeyance'). Bond - grievance, in Washington's own telling: a trade relationship 'fundamentally unbalanced' since 1979, 'grand-scale intellectual property theft', fentanyl precursors - the NSS writes the wound into the strategy. Mirrors CHN's grade of the US (rival, warming, grievance).

The structure has not moved: Washington is still the author of the sanctions (extended Feb 2025; Rosneft and Lukoil listed 22 Oct 2025; a Senate act authorising 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil passed 86-11), the supplier of the Patriots Ukraine fires (through PURL) and, since Ankara (Jul 2026), of a production licence; New START was allowed to expire on 5 Feb 2026 with no successor. Warming measured from 2024; the Rubio-Lavrov exchange of June 2026 ('a proposal, not an agreement') marks the ceiling. Bond - none: Trump's Washington treats Moscow as a deal counterpart; the grievance (2016, Ukraine) belongs to Congress and to Europe, not to the White House, which is why the bond is asymmetric with Moscow's own 'grievance'. Mirrors RUS's grade of the US (rival, warming).

stances.note: The one 'adversary' of the card and the test case for the grade. For: Washington opened a war on 28 Feb 2026 whose stated reasons, in the President's own statement, included regime change; Trump had called for regime change on 17 Jan ('it's time'); the first strikes killed the Supreme Leader; a naval blockade was imposed on 13 Apr and reinstated on 13 Jul after a signed memorandum (17 Jun) collapsed; Tehran's new leader promises vengeance 'until fully achieved'. The NSS wants Gulf energy kept from 'an outright enemy' - its one use of the word. Against: Hegseth said it was not 'a so-called regime-change war', the June memorandum and the October demands (a 'meaningful' cut in enrichment, Hormuz reopened) are the terms of a settlement, and the State Department's legal note frames the operation as self-defence. The atlas reads it as a war between two states each of which would accept the other's defeat, with talks as an instrument of the war; if a settlement on enrichment and Hormuz holds, the grade becomes rival. Stable: the aim has not moved since February while the means have (blockade, strikes, memorandum, strikes again). Bond - grievance: 1979, the embassy, Beirut 1983, and now the base attacks (6,700 missiles and drones on US-hosting states by May 2026). Mirrors IRN's grade of the US (adversary, stable, grievance).

stances_toward.note: Brazil's side of a pair the US card reads as rival (USA stance toward BRA, same sources). Brasilia cooperates out of necessity - the US is the market that the 2025 tariff and the 2026 Section 301 duty target - and resists alignment: it condemned the US removal of Maduro in January 2026 as an 'unacceptable line'. Warming on the same facts as the USA card: the Moraes delisting of 12 Dec 2025 and the partial rollback of the tariff. Bond - grievance: the 50% tariff was imposed over the Bolsonaro trial, an open wound. No Brazilian official statement on the tariff itself is cited here; the grade is a reading, confidence C. Sharpened 2026-10-16: the trend is moved from warming to stable. The sources read after the first draft contradict a thaw: the 7 May 2026 Lula-Trump meeting set a 30-day window for the tariffs, yet the 25% Section 301 duty still came on 15 July (in force from 22 July, with a separate 12.5% forced-labour surcharge reported), Brazil is preparing a response under its Reciprocity Law, Lula barred the US official Darren Beattie in March after he sought to visit Jair Bolsonaro in prison, and the defence minister said on 4 August that Brazil could not stop a US invasion. Beef, coffee, aircraft and rare earths are exempt from the new duty, so it is not a rupture. The USA card still reads warming on its own side; the two trends differ on purpose.
